entities.summary: Giora Romm was an Israeli military officer who served as deputy commander of the Israeli Air Force (IAF), Israel's military attaché in the United States and as director of the Civil Aviation Authority of Israel. Romm was the Israeli Air Force's first fighter jet ace, scoring five victories during the 1967 Six-Day War. In 1969, during the War of Attrition, Romm was shot down and spent several months in Egyptian captivity. He commanded the IAF's 115 Squadron through the intensive fighting of the 1973 Yom Kippur War and participated in Operation Wooden Leg, the 1985 raid against PLO headquarters in Tunisia.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: As Israel's first fighter jet ace and commander of the IAF's 115 Squadron during the 1973 Yom Kippur War, Romm played a crucial role in repelling the Egyptian attack. His leadership and combat skills significantly contributed to Israel's victory.
